newsitem.title: USA: Senate votes to expand campaign funds probe.
newsitem.headline: Senate votes to expand campaign funds probe.

text.p: The Senate voted unanimously Tuesday to expand its investigation of campaign fundraising abuses from just illegal actions to both illegal and improper activities.

The vote was 99 to 0 to expand the probe by the Senate Governmental Affairs committee in a victory for minority Democrats who forced Republicans, who control the Senate, to back down from their insistence on a probe only into illegal activities.

Sen. Christopher Dodd, a Connecticut Democrat and former chairman of the Democratic Party, abstained from the voting. The party is embroiled in a controversy over questionable and illegal foreign donations.

The key vote for expansion of the investigation came on an amendment to a measure to give the committee headed by Tennessee Republican Sen. Fred Thompson $4.35 million to examine fundraising activities with the focus on donations to Democrats for President Bill Clinton's 1996 campaign.
Democrats wanted the investigation expanded to cover congressional campaigns.

The vote followed negotiations after it became clear that the Republicans lacked the votes to win Senate approval only to look at illegal activities, which would have precluded a probe of millions of dollars raised in legal but possibly improper "soft money" donations.
